Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed mass with sharp margins in the right upper lung/pleural region. This smooth, non-infiltrative border is a characteristic radiographic feature of Pleuropulmonary Synovial Sarcoma (PPSS), helping to distinguish it from primary lung carcinomas which typically present with irregular, spiculated borders.
